The framework integrates structured and unstructured data, leveraging advanced Transformer architectures to capture temporal dynamics and complex interactions within the data. In a healthcare use case, the framework demonstrated its effectiveness by achieving an Accuracy of 0.854, an F1-Score of 0.895, and an AUC-ROC of 0.930, significantly outperforming traditional models. By incorporating SHAP for interpretability, the framework ensures that its predictions are both accurate and transparent, making it a valuable tool for decision-makers. While healthcare is one application, the framework's flexibility allows it to be adapted to a wide range of industries. Future work will focus on validating the framework across different sectors and integrating it into operational workflows to optimize decision-making and outcomes.

articleTitle: Multitask Sequence-to-Sequence Learning for Preprocessing Medical Textstable
publicationTitle: 2025 19th International Conference on Ubiquitous Information Management and Communication (IMCOM)
abstract: When medical texts become important and utilized more and more in many activities by both human and machines, medical text preprocessing is needed. On the other hand, medical text preprocessing often grapples with the hurdles of abbreviations and spelling errors. It would be time-consuming and less effectiveness if each of such problems in medical text preprocessing is overcome in sequence independently. For example, abbreviation expansion is handled and then spelling error correction is tackled or vice versa. Nonetheless, no existing work has taken into account medical text preprocessing in its entirety. In this paper, we propose to explore a multitask learning framework to harness the synergistic relationship between the subtasks in medical text preprocessing for better performance in terms of both efficiency and effectiveness. In particular, we define a novel multitask sequence-to-sequence model that can work on both abbreviation expansion and spelling error correction simultaneously. Using a shared representation approach, our model is composed of one BiLSTM-based encoder to represent the input and two BiLSTM-based decoders with the attention mechanism for subtask-specific processing. Trained on both subtasks at the same time, our model exploits the inherent connection between the two subtasks, leading to improved performance. Indeed, the experimental results on MeDAL dataset with many subdatasets of varying sentence lengths have confirmed the better performance of our model compared to that of any sequence combination of two single-task models running sequentially for abbreviation expansion and spelling error correction on medical texts.

articleTitle: Investigating the Technology Acceptance of QRIS Payment Among Indonesian Generation X
publicationTitle: 2025 19th International Conference on Ubiquitous Information Management and Communication (IMCOM)
abstract: The rapid advancement of technology and the shift towards a cashless society have led people to embrace cashless transactions. This transition is crucial for driving inclusive and sustainable national economic growth. One notable initiative is the implementation of the Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS), a standardized QR code accepted as a valid payment method in Indonesia. However, adopting QRIS in Indonesia faces challenges, including the varying levels of understanding of cashless payments across different generations. Each generation responds to technology differently, with Generation X shows greater adaptability. Therefore, this study aims to explore how Generation X accepts QRIS as a new technology and to analyze the key factors influencing its adoption by drawing on the diffusion of innovation theory. This study uses a quantitative approach by distributing the questionnaire to 100 respondents. The results were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 27 Software. It was found that the innovation represented by four indicators of the diffusion of innovation theory significantly influenced the adoption of QRIS. These findings align with SDG 9 on industry, innovation, and infrastructure. Thus, this study provides insights into generation-focused strategies to encourage more effective and widespread QRIS adoption.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Reasoning Framework to Detect Fake News on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2025 19th International Conference on Ubiquitous Information Management and Communication (IMCOM)
abstract: The rapid growth of social media has made the Internet a critical platform for spreading misinformation, which shapes public opinion and harms society. Despite significant research in fake news detection, most probabilistic efforts rely heavily on Naive Bayes, with limited exploration of other probabilistic models. This paper introduces a Bayesian network (BN) modelling-based framework for fake news detection, offering a probabilistic estimate of the likelihood of news being false. Unlike binary classification, this approach reflects human decision-making by evaluating three key questions: “who”, “what”, and “when”. Each module corresponds to a specific feature set, enabling nuanced reasoning about the news's credibility. The framework is flexible, allowing adjustments through expert input, knowledge bases, or real-world data. We validate the approach using a semi-synthetic dataset containing features from news content, user behaviour, and social context. The results highlight the framework's capacity to leverage expert knowledge, providing a more reliable and adaptive solution compared to traditional classifiers. The BN-based method demonstrates enhanced robustness, positioning it as a promising tool for tackling misinformation in an evolving digital landscape.

articleTitle: Imitating Mistakes in a Learning Companion AI Agent for Online Peer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 19th International Conference on Ubiquitous Information Management and Communication (IMCOM)
abstract: In recent years, peer learning has gained attention as a method that promotes spontaneous thinking among learners, and its effectiveness has been confirmed by numerous studies. This study aims to develop an AI Agent as a learning companion that enables peer learning anytime and anywhere. However, peer learning between humans has various limitations, and it is not always effective. Effective peer learning requires companions at the same proficiency levels. In this study, we assume that a learner's peers with the same proficiency level as the learner make the same mistakes as the learner does and focus on English composition as a specific example to validate this approach.

articleTitle: EMMAR: Exploration of Malaysian Traditional Musical Instrument with Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2025 19th International Conference on Ubiquitous Information Management and Communication (IMCOM)
abstract: This paper aims to enhance visitor engagement at the Malaysian Musical Museum (Muzium Muzik Malaysia) by developing an augmented reality (AR) mobile application, EMMAR, using the Unity game engine. The application uses a booklet to provide interactive educational experiences with traditional Malaysian musical instruments, which are typically off-limits for touching. The goal is to improve visitor participation and appreciation of the museum's cultural heritage, leveraging AR technology to create dynamic, hands-on interactions. The study employs the ADDIE research methodology, combining qualitative and quantitative techniques. It includes a sample of 80 respondents, primarily museum visitors and university students, targeting younger and urban participants. Key findings reveal that university students show higher adaptability to augmented reality, while general museum visitors remain neutral towards the use of advanced technology in museum exhibitions.

articleTitle: Error Detection of BERT-Based Bibliographic Information Extraction from Reference Strings
publicationTitle: 2025 19th International Conference on Ubiquitous Information Management and Communication (IMCOM)
abstract: Extracting bibliographic information, such as titles and authors, from reference strings is indispensable for generating inter-document links in digital libraries. Thus, we have developed a BERT-based bibliographic information extraction method for reference strings. Although the extraction accuracy was competitive, labor-intensive manual error correction is in-evitable after the extraction. Therefore, we propose a method to detect reference strings that are highly likely to contain extraction errors in order to reduce the manual post-editing. We also use multiple natural language processing models other than BERT to extract bibliographic information from reference strings and detect extraction errors. In our experiments, we present the bibliographic information extraction accuracy of multiple models as well as the accuracy of detecting erroneous reference strings. Specifically, in experiments involving reference strings from an English journal, XLM-RoBERTa achieved a bibliographic information extraction accuracy of 0.958 and detected 89.0% of reference strings containing extraction errors. These detected reference strings represented 13.7% of the total. If all the detected reference strings are assumed to be manually corrected, the accuracy of bibliographic information improves to 0.995.
